topic: Semiconservative Replication, Replication Fork Enzymes, & DNA Pol III/I
quickSummary: Meselson & Stahl (1958): CsCl density gradient centrifugation proved semiconservative replication. summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Meselson & Stahl (1958) used 15N/14N isotope equilibrium density gradient centrifugation in CsCl to prove semiconservative DNA replication. Replication proceeds 5'->3'. Key enzymes in E. coli: DnaB Helicase, SSBs, DNA Gyrase (Topoisomerase II), DnaG Primase, DNA Polymerase III (main replicase with 3'->5' proofreading), DNA Polymerase I (primer removal via 5'->3' exonuclease), and DNA Ligase.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MESELSON & STAHL EXPERIMENT (1958)
                      
   Generation 0: Grown on ¹⁵NH₄Cl (Heavy) ──► Single Heavy Band (¹⁵N-¹⁵N)
                                                     │
   Generation 1: Transferred to ¹⁴NH₄Cl ──► Single Hybrid Intermediate Band (¹⁵N-¹⁴N)
                                                     │
   Generation 2: Continued on ¹⁴NH₄Cl    ──► 50% Hybrid Band (¹⁵N-¹⁴N) + 50% Light Band (¹⁴N-¹⁴N)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 4.1 Meselson & Stahl Experiment (1958)
- Proved that DNA replication is **semiconservative** (each daughter DNA molecule conserves one parental strand and synthesizes one new strand).
- **Isotope Tracking in *E. coli***:
  - Gen 0 ($^{15}\text{N}$): $100\%$ Heavy ($^{15}\text{N-}^{15}\text{N}$).
  - Gen 1 ($1^{\text{st}}$ generation in $^{14}\text{N}$): $100\%$ Hybrid ($^{15}\text{N-}^{14}\text{N}$).
  - Gen 2 ($2^{\text{nd}}$ generation in $^{14}\text{N}$): $50\%$ Hybrid + $50\%$ Light ($^{14}\text{N-}^{14}\text{N}$).
  - Gen 3 ($3^{\text{rd}}$ generation in $^{14}\text{N}$): $25\%$ Hybrid + $75\%$ Light ($2\text{ Hybrid} : 6\text{ Light}$).

### 4.2 Enzymatic Machinery at the Replication Fork

```
                       REPLICATION FORK ARCHITECTURE
                       
                           3' ─────────────────── 5' (Leading Template)
                                \   Continuous
                                 \  5' ────────► 3' (Leading Strand)
     Unwinding by                 \
   DnaB Helicase ────────────► \
   (Stabilized by SSBs)           /  3' ◄─── 5' (Okazaki Fragment)
                                 /   Discontinuous
                                /    5' ────────── 3' (Lagging Template)
```

| Replication Enzyme | Function in *E. coli* (Prokaryotes) | Eukaryotic Homologue |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DNA Helicase** | **DnaB**; unwinds double helix using ATP | **MCM Complex** |
| **SSBs** | **SSB**; prevents single strand re-annealing | **RPA** |
| **Topoisomerase** | **DNA Gyrase** (Type II); relieves positive supercoiling ahead of fork | **Topoisomerase I & II** |
| **Primase** | **DnaG**; synthesizes short RNA primers ($10\text{--}12\text{ nt}$) | **DNA Pol $\alpha$ / Primase** |
| **Main Replicase** | **DNA Polymerase III** ($5' \rightarrow 3'$ synthesis $+ 3' \rightarrow 5'$ proofreading) | **DNA Pol $\delta$ / $\epsilon$** |
| **Primer Removal** | **DNA Polymerase I** (unique **$5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease** activity) | **FEN1 $+ \text{DNA Pol }\delta$** |
| **DNA Ligase** | Seals phosphodiester nicks using $\text{NAD}^+$ | **DNA Ligase I** (uses ATP) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Taylor's Vicia faba Experiment
conceptBreakdown.title: Taylor's Vicia faba Experiment
conceptBreakdown.content: J. Herbert Taylor (1958) demonstrated semiconservative replication in eukaryotic chromosomes of broad bean (Vicia faba) root tip cells using radioactive tritiated thymidine (^3H-thymidine) and autoradiography.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Trombone Model of the Replisome
conceptBreakdown.title: Trombone Model of the Replisome
conceptBreakdown.content: The dimeric DNA Pol III holoenzyme coordinates leading and lagging strand synthesis simultaneously by looping the lagging strand template through the replisome in a trombone-like cycle.
